1. a short, large-displacement fundamental-shear excursion that contributes to enhanced magnetic diffusion; and
2. a common velocity erasure followed by a short unforced smoothing interval.

The second operation controls the velocity generated by the Lorentz force. Magnetic diffusion remains active throughout both operations. A quantitative averaging argument gives contraction of the resulting magnetic evolution in operator norm; a single global Duhamel estimate then controls its nonlinear induction term.
